claims.text: Language models make it cheap to write decision policies, five, a hundred, two hundred, and that moves the bottleneck to sign-off, because no head of support can read and approve two hundred properly.
claims.quote: That is new, and useful, and it moves the bottleneck. The bottleneck is now sign-off.

claims.text: A sign-off without the time to read is the rubber stamp this site describes in agency is not a yes: liability, not agency.
claims.quote: a sign-off without the time to read is the rubber stamp

claims.text: How can a large number of decisions be approved without anyone reading most of them?
claims.quote: So the question is how to approve a large number of decisions without anyone reading most of them.

claims.text: Decisions sit at altitudes, strategic, business, product, technical and the single run, each with its own decisions and workflows, and each level bounded by the one above; the shape is a fractal semantic graph.
claims.quote: What matters is that each level is bounded by the one above it.

claims.text: The scaling rule: you sign off at an altitude, and everything below inherits it; the board approves a risk appetite, not the refund tool.
claims.quote: You sign off at an altitude, and everything below inherits it.

claims.text: The UK Corporate Governance Code's Principle O asks the board to determine the nature and extent of the principal risks it is willing to take, and ISO Guide 73 calls that risk appetite.
claims.quote: determine the nature and extent of the principal risks the company is willing to take in order to achieve its long-term strategic objectives

claims.text: The FRC's guidance asks boards for a formal schedule of matters reserved for their decision, to give clarity over where responsibility for decision-making lies; approving at altitude is that, carried down to agents.
claims.quote: Approving at altitude is that, carried down to agents.

claims.text: Each sign-off is small because each level only reads its own level; two hundred decision policies at the bottom are fine if every one fits inside the few read and approved above it.
claims.quote: Each sign-off is small, because each level only has to read its own level.

claims.text: The rule that makes inheritance safe: a lower level may narrow the level above it, and it may never widen it.
claims.quote: A lower level may narrow the level above it. It may never widen it.

claims.text: English law has a name for widening: a statutory instrument that goes beyond the power its Act gave is ultra vires, and a court can quash it.
claims.quote: A rule that goes beyond it is ultra vires, outside the powers, and a court can quash it.

claims.text: On 26 July 2017 the Supreme Court quashed the employment tribunal fees order in R (UNISON) v Lord Chancellor, holding it unlawful ab initio because the Act gave power to set fees but not fees that prevented access to justice.
claims.quote: the court held the order "unlawful ab initio", from the start, and said it "must be quashed".

claims.text: Every policy declares an envelope with the same fields at every altitude: money, blast radius, data in scope, people in scope, reversibility and duration, which is what makes the levels comparable.
claims.quote: The point is that the fields are the same at every level. That is what makes the levels comparable

claims.text: Where the envelope is numbers and lists, the check that a child fits inside its parent is mechanical, needs no model, and can run in CI on every change to a policy.
claims.quote: That check is deterministic, needs no model, and can run in CI on every change to a policy

claims.text: Where the envelope is words, a model can flag likely conflicts for a person to decide; it widens what a person can review and does not replace the review.
claims.quote: it widens what a person can review, it does not replace the review.

claims.text: The illustrative case is a VIP workflow refunding up to 1,000 GBP without a person, wider than the business limit of 100 GBP an order, so it is flagged as out of its powers before it runs.
claims.quote: The illustrative case in the figure is a "VIP" workflow that refunds up to 1,000 GBP without a person.

value.unit: GBP automatic refund limit proposed against the business limit

claims.text: A decision far outside the risk appetite shows up as an envelope that does not fit inside its parent's, whoever wrote it, which is how a business finds what nobody predicted.
claims.quote: A decision far outside its risk appetite shows up as an envelope that does not fit inside its parent's

claims.text: A kill switch sits at the altitude whose envelope it protects, escalation goes up one altitude, and a licence to operate is an envelope with a name.
claims.quote: A kill switch sits at the altitude whose envelope it protects.

claims.text: The 2,000 GBP daily circuit breaker belongs to the business level: it stops all automatic refunds, not one agent.
claims.quote: The 2,000 GBP daily circuit breaker belongs to the business level: it stops all automatic refunds, not one agent.

value.unit: GBP a day of automatic refunds

claims.text: Somebody still has to write the top: a risk appetite that says nothing measurable cannot be checked against, and the mechanical check is only as good as the numbers at the top.
claims.quote: The mechanical check is only as good as the numbers at the top.

claims.text: Envelopes can be gamed: a team can split one large refund into several small ones, so the envelope needs aggregate limits like the daily breaker, not only per-case ones.
claims.quote: A team can split one large refund into several small ones.

claims.text: Altitude is not hierarchy: the levels follow what is decided, not the org chart, and the person who owns a limit may not be the most senior.
claims.quote: The levels follow what is decided, not the org chart; the person who owns a limit may not be the most senior.

claims.text: Words stay hard: the model's flags are suggestions, and the decision is a person's.
claims.quote: The model's flags are suggestions; the decision is a person's.

claims.text: It is a proposal: no decision-policy format with envelopes exists yet, and the fields are the owner's.
claims.quote: No decision-policy format with envelopes exists yet; the fields above are mine.

claims.text: The numbers are illustrative: the tool's limits come from the third design in Hope or enforcement, and the levels above them are made up for the example.
claims.quote: the levels above them are made up for the example.

claims.text: The legal parallel is an analogy: courts and CI are different things, and the article borrows the shape, not the authority.
claims.quote: Courts and CI are different things; the article borrows the shape, not the authority.

claims.text: This is the second of four articles on agent decision policies, written from a voice memo of 17 October 2026 and checked by the site's agent, with editorial responsibility the owner's.
claims.quote: A voice memo from me on 17 October 2026, written up and checked by this site's agent; the editorial responsibility is mine.
